zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two attribute values (e.g., 'the Swedish person is the person who loves cooking'), treat them as a single linked entity and assign them together.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains an equality or equivalence between two attribute values.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'Swedish = cooking' as two independent facts and placing Swedish nationality and cooking hobby in different houses.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, place that attribute at that house right away.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'X is in the Nth house' or 'X is not in the Nth house' (the latter as a direct exclusion).
zebralogic.example: Delaying placement of 'the rose bouquet is not in the sixth house' and later assigning roses to house 6.

zebralogic.title: Translate 'N houses between' to Exact Distance
zebralogic.principle: Convert statements like 'there are N houses between X and Y' into the exact distance constraint |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two entities.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'there is one house between Peter and the mystery book' as only 'Peter is left of mystery' and ignoring the required distance of two houses.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Translate 'next to', 'directly left of', and similar phrasing into precise adjacency constraints (|pos(A) - pos(B)| = 1) with correct ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses adjacency language.
zebralogic.example: Placing 'British directly left of Carol' with a gap between them.

zebralogic.title: Treat Consecutive Chains as a Block
zebralogic.principle: When several adjacency clues form a sequence (e.g., A left of B left of C), treat the whole sequence as a block to reduce search space.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When multiple adjacency constraints involve the same set of entities forming a chain.
zebralogic.example: Handling 'German < woodworking < daffodils' as separate constraints instead of a single ordered block.

zebralogic.title: Propagate Linked Attribute Pairs
zebralogic.principle: Whenever a clue links two attributes of the same entity (e.g., 'Carol uses OnePlus 9'), immediately propagate the link so both attributes are assigned together.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue states that a name is associated with a specific attribute value.
zebralogic.example: Failing to link 'Alice drinks Blueberry smoothies' with Alice's name, treating them as unrelated.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: Produce a JSON object with top‑level keys 'header' (list of column names) and 'rows' (list of rows), matching the verifier's expected schema.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of solving, before returning the answer.
zebralogic.example: Returning a JSON with a top‑level 'solution' key instead of 'header' and 'rows'.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: Limit explanatory text before the final JSON so that the total output stays within the model's token limit.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When the reasoning is becoming lengthy; keep it brief.
zebralogic.example: Including a long step‑by‑step deduction that exceeds the token budget, causing the JSON to be cut off.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values verbatim from the problem statement, preserving exact case, spacing, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final solution, use the exact strings as given.
zebralogic.example: Writing 'German' instead of 'german' in the output.

zebralogic.title: Directional Ordering for 'somewhere to the left/right of' constraints
zebralogic.principle: Translate clues that state 'X is somewhere to the left/right of Y' into strict ordering constraints (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like 'X is somewhere to the left of Y' or 'X is somewhere to the right of Y'.
zebralogic.example: Placing Carol left of Mountain despite the clue 'Carol is somewhere to the right of Mountain'.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing the output to exceed the token limit and truncate the JSON solution.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to include exhaustive step‑by‑step deduction, which can exceed the token budget.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep the reasoning brief and place the final JSON near the end of the output.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier (e.g., missing 'header'/'rows' keys or adding extra wrapper fields).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may output a different JSON schema or add extra fields.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Follow the exact expected schema with only 'header' and 'rows' at the top level.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values (e.g., 'German' instead of 'german').
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or forgets to preserve the original token spelling.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute tokens verbatim from the problem statement.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting adjacency constraints that involve a named entity and a non‑name attribute (e.g., child name), treating them as non‑adjacent or placing both in the same house.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may treat name‑attribute adjacency as a direct equivalence rather than an adjacency relation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply adjacency rules correctly even when one side is a name.
